_comment: CURRENT-SYLLABUS LAYER. Built 2026-08-21 from the official slide deck's five block descriptions, supplied by the user. This is the authority on WHAT is examinable; the past papers remain the authority on HOW questions are asked. Re-run archetypes_postprocess.py after editing.
status: BUILT from block summaries + exercise notebooks + slide-level lecture summaries
built_from: UNION of three sources: (1) the 5 slide block summaries, (2) exercises/*.ipynb, (3) lectures/_summaries/*.txt - slide-level summaries of the actual deck. Staff named slides AND exercises as the study basis, so the examinable set is the union, never the intersection.
caveat: Built from block-level SUMMARIES, not the full slide-by-slide table of contents. A topic named in a summary is certainly current. A topic absent from a summary is probably but not certainly gone - hence the `at_risk` status rather than `dropped`.

form_vs_content._comment: The staff message invalidates one half of the archetype model and explicitly endorses the other. Keeping them apart is the whole point of this file.

form_layer.confidence: CONFIRMED from the current official slides (2026-08-21): 'Written exam, duration 90min, closed book' - identical to the 2023 paper. Staff say the CONTENT changed; the FORM provably did not. That is direct evidence for this split, not just a premise.
covers: exam duration, mark total, question count
playbook.answer_shape and the 'marks = number of distinct scorable statements' rule
format mix (explain_derive dominant) and mean marks per question
generic traps: justify every yes/no, match step count to marks, answer both halves

content_layer.anchored_on: the official slide blocks (this file), as of 2026-08-21
content_layer.confidence: GOOD for presence/absence of topics. Mark weights are still past-paper-derived and remain approximate.
covers: which archetypes exist in the first place

status_values.current: named in the slide blocks - full weight
status_values.at_risk: absent from the slide block that covers its area, while sibling topics in that block ARE named. Weight 0.5: kept in the queue but demoted. Not dropped, because the source is a summary, and under-drilling a topic that turns out to be examined costs far more than over-drilling one that isn't.
status_values.unverified: no evidence either way - full weight, flagged
status_values.new: named in the slides but absent from EVERY past paper - a BLIND SPOT. No past-paper exemplar exists, so any archetype is built from the syllabus plus the confirmed form rules.

Image Filtering and Convolution.evidence: linear filters, pixel-wise operations, noise reduction (Gaussian and salt-and-pepper), cross-correlation vs convolution via 180-degree kernel flip, Gaussian Pyramids with smoothing before downsampling to prevent aliasing

Edge Detection.evidence: image gradients / Sobel; full Canny chain: Gaussian smoothing, gradient magnitude and orientation, Non-Maximum Suppression, double thresholding + hysteresis. Hough Transform with r = x cos(theta) + y sin(theta) given explicitly.
Edge Detection.emphasis: The slides state the Hough voting equation explicitly - expect it to be examined as a formula, not just described.

Feature Detection and Description.evidence: Harris corner detector, eigenvalues of the second-moment matrix M classifying flat/edge/corner; automatic scale selection via scale-normalized LoG; 128-dim SIFT descriptor from gradient-orientation histograms

Homography and Image Alignment.evidence: NOT NAMED in any block. Block 5 covers camera calibration, epipolar geometry, E/F matrices, the normalized 8-point algorithm, triangulation and RANSAC - but never homography, image alignment, stitching or panoramas.
Homography and Image Alignment.action: CHECK THE SLIDE TOC for 'homography', 'image alignment', 'panorama', 'warping'. This gates derive-homography-A, a must-cover archetype worth 7 marks in the 2023 paper - the single most consequential uncertainty in this file.
Homography and Image Alignment.note_2: Also absent from every exercise. But the block summaries proved INCOMPLETE (they omitted transformers, which the exercises show are taught), so absence from a summary is weaker evidence than it first appeared. Kept at at_risk 0.5 rather than demoted further.
Homography and Image Alignment.note_3: 6_local_features covers 'Application: Image Matching' (slides 23-26) and 'Application: Image Stitching' (slides 27-30). Stitching IS homography estimation, so the capability is taught even though the word is absent from the summaries. Kept at at_risk 0.5 rather than lowered.

Image Segmentation with MRF and Graph Cu.evidence: MRF energy minimization, unary (data likelihood) vs pairwise (spatial consistency) potentials, s-t mincut/maxflow for binary labelling, GrabCut with interactive brush strokes

RANSAC and Robust Estimation.evidence: 'RANSAC is integrated throughout as a robust iterative estimator to filter out outlier point correspondences'

Clustering and Mixture Models.evidence: K-Means as unsupervised pixel-wise clustering; Mixture of Gaussians optimized via Expectation-Maximization
Clustering and Mixture Models.content_shift: MEAN-SHIFT IS NOT NAMED. Block 2 contrasts K-Means with MoG/EM specifically. In the 2022 paper Mean-Shift was an entire 11-mark question. Conversely EM is named and has no past-paper coverage at all - see the new topic below. The topic survives; its centre of gravity moved from Mean-Shift to EM.
Clustering and Mixture Models.note_2: k-Means appears in image_segmentation; Mean-Shift appears only in the DETECTION summaries (cnn_1, feature_detection), never in image_segmentation. EM/MoG is the segmentation centrepiece (slides 9-15). Mean-Shift is de-emphasised, not proven absent.

Sliding-Window Object Detection.evidence: sliding-window over image pyramids, multiple scales and locations; HOG descriptor chain; cascading classifiers; region proposal generation

Support Vector Machines.evidence: linear SVM classification as the final stage of the HOG pipeline

Boosting and Ensemble Classifiers.evidence: Viola-Jones weak classifiers optimized via boosting, cascading classifiers for search efficiency

Convolutional Neural Networks.evidence: CNN vs MLP via local connectivity and shared weights; conv layers, ReLU, BatchNorm, pooling; receptive field analysis; dilated convolutions

Neural Network Training and Loss Functio.evidence: loss functions covered, but the named one is TRIPLET LOSS
Neural Network Training and Loss Functio.content_shift: Past papers examined cross-entropy (2023 Q5e) and L1 (mockup Q5c). The slides name triplet loss with anchor-positive/anchor-negative distances and hard mining. Keep the formula-and-gloss drill, but triplet loss is now the likeliest instance.

Semantic Segmentation with Deep Learning.evidence: Fully Convolutional Networks, encoder-decoder architectures SegNet and U-Net, skip connections preserving high-resolution detail

Camera Models and Projection.evidence: pinhole model and calibration; intrinsic matrix with focal length, skew and principal point; extrinsic rotation and translation. Block 1 additionally names the THIN LENS model.
Camera Models and Projection.content_shift: Thin lens model appears in Block 1 and in no past paper - see the new topic below.

Stereo Vision and Epipolar Geometry.evidence: epipolar geometry; Essential matrix (calibrated) vs Fundamental matrix (uncalibrated); normalized 8-point algorithm; linear triangulation of X = (a,b,c)
Stereo Vision and Epipolar Geometry.emphasis: The slides say NORMALIZED 8-point algorithm explicitly - the normalisation step is examinable, not optional trivia.

Structure from Motion.evidence: NOT NAMED. Block 5 ends at triangulation and RANSAC; no bundle adjustment, no multi-view reconstruction, no projective SfM.
Structure from Motion.action: Gates derive-sfm-dof (2 marks in 2023). Low stakes - demote and move on.

Metric Learning and Triplet Embeddings.evidence: 'matching and retrieval tasks are modeled using Siamese networks, triplet embeddings, and triplet loss to minimize distance between anchor-positive pairs and maximize it for anchor-negative pairs, optimized through online hard triplet mining variants like batch hard or batch all'
Metric Learning and Triplet Embeddings.note: BIGGEST BLIND SPOT. An entire named sub-area of Block 4 with zero coverage in any past paper. Detailed enough in the slides (batch hard vs batch all) to be examined at depth.

Deformable Part-based Models.evidence: 'Deformable Part-based Models (DPM) extend this approach by modeling objects as a hierarchical configuration of a coarse root filter and multiple higher-resolution part filters, scoring hypotheses by combining HOG filter matches with geometric deformation costs'
Deformable Part-based Models.note: Named with mechanism. No past-paper coverage.

Multi-scale Dense Prediction (FPN, ASPP).evidence: 'Feature Pyramid Networks (FPN) and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) are presented for multi-scale dense prediction'
Multi-scale Dense Prediction (FPN, ASPP).note: No past-paper coverage. Adjacent to the covered encoder-decoder material, so cheaper to close than the others.

Expectation-Maximization for Mixture Mod.evidence: 'probabilistic classification using Mixture of Gaussians (MoG) models optimized via the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm'
Expectation-Maximization for Mixture Mod.note: MoG appears in the 2023 paper only as a distractor ('why would MoG be a poor choice'). The EM algorithm itself - E-step, M-step, convergence - is never examined in any past paper, yet it is the named optimiser in the current slides. Classic 'list the steps' target.

Thin Lens Model.evidence: 'how physical scenes are projected onto digital sensors via pinhole and thin lens models'
Thin Lens Model.note: Minor. Past papers cover the pinhole/intrinsic matrix only.

Region Proposals.evidence: 'search efficiency is optimized using cascading classifiers ... or region proposal generation to focus computation on likely object locations'
Region Proposals.note: Minor, and adjacent to the covered cascade material.

Vision Transformers and Self-Attention.evidence: Exercise 4: Positional Encoding (sin/cos formula given), Self-Attention softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V, Transformer block z'=MSA(LN(z))+z, ViT assembly with class token, patchify T and D formulas.
Vision Transformers and Self-Attention.note: STRONGEST-EVIDENCED blind spot: exercised in depth, and the exercise text asks conceptual questions about it directly.

Residual Networks and Training Practices.evidence: Exercise 4: residual blocks and identity shortcuts, global average pooling, learning-rate decay, L2/weight decay; Exercise 3: Adam, data augmentation, ReLU.
Residual Networks and Training Practices.note: Exercise 4 works a receptive-field-with-stride answer explicitly (3 -> 7 -> 15).

Attention Mechanisms.evidence: 7_reconstruction: scaled dot-product attention softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V, alignment E=QK^T, masked attention, multi-head, self- vs cross-attention, why an MLP is needed between attention layers.

Transformers for Detection and Segmentat.evidence: 7_reconstruction: DETR (set prediction, no NMS), Mask2Former, EoMT + mask annealing, DynaMITe interactive segmentation, CNNs vs mask transformers.

Self-Supervised and Multimodal Learning.evidence: 7_reconstruction: pretext tasks, self-supervised learning, contrastive learning, CLIP and shared embedding spaces, multimodal token streams.

Human Pose Estimation with FCNs.evidence: 5_transformers slides 4-9: FCNs for pose, heat-map predictions, OpenPose, 3D body pose, CNN + differentiable geometry.
Human Pose Estimation with FCNs.note: Not archetyped - accepted risk, likely a short recall item.

Backpropagation and Optimisation.evidence: cnn_1 part 2: loss functions, regularization terms, backpropagation, stochastic vs batch, minibatches, learning rate.

corrections_forced_by_the_slides: HOG uses 9 ORIENTATION BINS and 8x8 cells per the current slides. The mockup paper's question used 8 bins, and the feature-vector-size-count playbook was written from it. Corrected in archetypes_map.py - this was a factual error that would have cost marks.
ASPP and atrous/dilated convolution appear in NO lecture summary while FPN does. The block summary named both. multiscale-dense-prediction narrowed to FPN and cut from 3 to 2 marks.
alpha-expansion (non-binary graph cuts) and augmenting-path max-flow added to mrf-graphcut-mechanics; the Generalized Distance Transform added to deformable-part-models.

exercise_evidence.why_they_matter: They are programming tasks, but their MARKDOWN cells carry conceptual questions in exactly the exam's voice - 'Which network has more parameters?', 'What is the size of the receptive field?', 'Why do we use addition instead of concatenation?', 'provide formulas to compute T and D'. Those conceptual prompts, not the code, are the archetype source.
exercise_evidence.biggest_find: Exercise 4 covers Vision Transformers in depth - patchify, positional encoding with its formula, self-attention softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V, the transformer block equations, class token. This appears in NO past paper AND was absent from the block summaries. It surfaced only from the exercises.
exercise_evidence.absent_from_exercises: triplet/Siamese, FPN/ASPP, EM/MoG/k-Means/Mean-Shift, DPM, homography, SfM, Viola-Jones/boosting/cascades, U-Net/SegNet/FCN. Exercises are the PRACTICAL subset, so absence here is weak evidence - it does not override a topic being named in the slides.

source_caveats.lecture_summaries_are_INCOMPLETE: CRITICAL. Absence from lectures/_summaries/ is NOT evidence of absence from the course. Epipolar geometry, Fundamental/Essential matrices, the 8-point algorithm, RANSAC and the Hough transform appear in NO summary - yet Block 5 names the first four explicitly and Block 1 gives the Hough voting equation verbatim. At least one summary is missing.
source_caveats.filenames_do_not_match_contents: 7_reconstruction.txt is TRANSFORMERS (attention -> ViT -> DETR/Mask2Former -> CLIP/SSL). 6_local_features.txt is 3D reconstruction, stereo, image matching/stitching, Harris, SIFT, SURF. 5_transformers.txt is FCN pose estimation + Siamese/triplet/contrastive. cnn_2.txt is a BYTE-IDENTICAL DUPLICATE of 5_transformers.txt, so a genuine 'CNN part 2' summary may be missing. Trust contents, not names.
source_caveats.consequence: Nothing is marked `dropped` anywhere in this file. With demonstrably incomplete sources, absence can never justify removing an archetype - only the `at_risk` demotion, which keeps it in the queue at half weight.
